rules.basis: English Wikipedia daily views (worldwide) of the title's article: one edition every title has. Reads, never viewers. A day counts only inside a stored per-article curve.
rules.release: Films — theatrical: the calendar, else Wikidata P577 (a platform's own film has none); OTT: the article's streaming date, or the platform original's premiere. Shows: premiere or a season's start — a series date with no other date in the 28 days before it (weekly episode / part dates are not releases).
rules.cohort: Rows = release week (Mon–Sun). Columns = days since release. Cell = mean % of each title's own peak (days 0..28; peak so far for a title still under 29 days). Needs ≥ 7 days after release.
rules.shape: Needs the curve to reach release + 21 days. p = peak day (0..28), r7 = views at p+7 ÷ peak. Front-loaded: p ≤ 3 and r7 < 35%. Slow burner: p > 6, or r7 ≥ 70%. Steady: otherwise.
rules.pctl: Percentile of 28-day reads (days 0..27) among the distinct titles of the same language released the same month (same lane and date basis; a title counts once). Needs ≥ 3 titles; 100 = the most read.
rules.fan: Wikidata P161 cast (first 10 billed) · P57 director · P179 part of the series · P54 current team · P1344 participant in. Heat = sum of members' 7-day reads (Indian editions + English worldwide for an Indian member, English from India for others, by Wikidata claims; ≥ = floor). A bare adult search word ('xXx') has no reads: they are adult searches.
rules.pull: A film released in the last 28 days vs its star: the film's English reads in the last 7 days ÷ the star's own median weekly English reads over the last 8 weeks. Above 1× = beating the star's usual pull.
rules.sport: Day 0 = a calendar fixture naming the athlete / team (or its team / event) — the fixture day its curve is highest — else its 60-day curve peak. Staying power = days from the peak (days 0..14) at ≥ 50% of it; '≥' = still above at the newest day.
rules.validation: Netflix's official India Top 10 (weekly): weeks per title or season run, finished runs only, vs the shape of its English Wikipedia curve from its Netflix release. Mann–Whitney U, two-sided. Counted in runs; two runs on the same release curve (e.g. two seasons matched to one release) count once.
